critique: The palette is violet, but the result is far too bright and saturated for a dark background-grade nebula, especially at t4 where most of the frame becomes electric purple. The cloud field has a clearly visible rectangular emitter boundary across the upper area and at the side edges, which breaks the no-hard-edges requirement. Within that rectangle the image is largely smooth and uniform rather than showing layered, cloud-like nebula structure; grain is only barely perceptible. Between t1 and t4 there is substantial overall brightening, but little readable internal morphing or drifting structure.

suggestions.why: Expand the Box emission volume well beyond the composition so its rectangular boundaries fall outside frame.
Reduce particle opacity substantially so additive accumulation remains dark violet instead of blooming into bright magenta.
Lower emission density to prevent the field from progressively filling into a flat, overbright solid color at later times.
Increase broad turbulent displacement so the visible density develops more distinct slow-moving gaseous variations rather than mainly changing overall brightness.
